## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR has one Critical defect to fix before merge. It deletes `app/defaults.json`, but `app/startup.py` still reads that file, so `load_defaults()` will now raise on every call. It also has three Important defects. `is_valid_port` rejects port 65535, which its docstring says is valid. `load_config` turns every failure into `{}` without any signal to the caller. The `normalize_host` docstring says empty input returns `None`, but the code returns `""`. The new trailing-dot branch in `normalize_host` also has no test.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — After this file is deleted, every call to `load_defaults()` in `app/startup.py:6` raises `FileNotFoundError`, because that function still does `json.loads(Path(__file__).with_name("defaults.json").read_text())`. The diff does not update `app/startup.py`, and no other file supplies `defaults.json`. Either keep `app/defaults.json`, or move `load_defaults` to a new source for its defaults (for example, inline `{"timeout": 30}`) in the same PR. — Any startup path that calls `load_defaults()` crashes with an unhandled `FileNotFoundError` instead of loading the default timeout of 30.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns `False`, even though the docstring says "True when p is a usable TCP port (1-65535)". The check `0 < p < 65535` excludes the upper bound. Change it to `0 < p <= 65535`, and add an upper-bound case to `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` or a new test that checks both 65535 and 65536. — Configurations that use port 65535, a legal TCP port, are rejected. The current tests check only 0, 1 and 8080, so they do not catch this.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — If `load_config` gets a missing path, an unreadable file or malformed JSON, it returns `{}`, and the caller cannot tell any of these apart from a valid empty config. `except Exception: return {}` swallows `FileNotFoundError`, `PermissionError`, and the JSON decode error from `json` or `ujson`. Nothing is logged, and no comment or docstring says the fallback is intentional. The docstring says only "Load the JSON config at path." Catch only the errors that should fall back (for example, `FileNotFoundError`), log them or document the fallback, and let parse errors reach the caller. — A typo in a config file or a wrong path quietly runs the application on built-in defaults, and operators get nothing to diagnose. No test exercises this error path either.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — `normalize_host("")` returns `""`, but the docstring says it "returns None when h is empty". Line 37 is `return ""`. Decide which contract is intended, then fix either the docstring or the return value and add a test for empty input. — Callers that follow the docstring and check `is None` treat an empty host as present, and nothing guards the empty-input branch against regressions.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — No test exercises the trailing-dot branch (`if lowered.endswith("."): lowered = lowered[:-1]`). `test_normalize_host_lowercases` passes only `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot. Add a case such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.") == "example.com"`. — A regression in the stripping of the fully qualified suffix, such as stripping every trailing dot or none, would go undetected.

## Strengths
- `test_parse_timeout_millis` exercises the new `ms` branch of `parse_timeout` with a value (`"1500ms"` → `1.5`) that would fail if the division or the suffix slicing were wrong.
- `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound` checks both sides of the lower boundary (0 rejected, 1 accepted).

## Not reviewed
(none)
